name: Abyss 0.8.1
body:
Abyss 0.8.1 fixes watchdog phase isolation, endpoint state lifetime, native send accounting, and public network-drop statistics while preserving the legacy API.

- Stale init/callback/effects watchdog expiry cannot terminate a later execution phase; current deadlines and settlement barriers remain enforced.
- Endpoint state and managed timers persist for the socket generation. Keyed idle eviction remains finite.
- Supported native sends record each actual local outcome once, independently of sampling. Admission rejection and receipt reads do not count as sends.
- Public drops reconcile ingress and runtime rejection without double-counting, remain available through drain, and separate rejected internal events.

Validation: Linux OTP 27/28 full integration, 688 tests and 3 doctests with zero final failures; Linux/macOS regression matrix; 19-job actual-wire/package matrix; strict compile, format, Dialyzer, documentation, overload bounds, and unchanged optional QUIC consumers. Strict Credo retains 83 baseline findings with none introduced. Controlled loopback samples show 3.3–8.1% median throughput declines across modes; these measured limits are documented.

[Hardening report and reproducible evidence](https://github.com/gsmlg-dev/abyss/blob/main/docs/udp-runtime/post-release-fixes.md).
